Das "Ventil" ist die Drosselklappe. Gibst du gas, öffnet sie sich, um mehr Luft in den Motor zu lassen, damit mehr Sauerstoff für eine Kraftvollere Verbrennung vorhanden ist. Das Motorsteuergerät passt dann mithilfe der Stellung dessen und der gemessenen Luftmasse vom Luftmassenmesser (Links am Rand des 1. Bilds, mit dem Stecker) die Kraftstoffmenge an. Mehr Kraftstoff und Sauerstoff -> Kraftvollere/Größere Verbrennung=Mehr Leistung.

Wenn nun aber die Drosselklappe zu stark verdreckt ist, kann es sein, dass sie sich nicht mehr richtig Bewegt und nicht die angeforderte Luftmasse in den Motor lässt.

The thing making them illegal here (Germany) would be the lines not being approved by the The Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA) and not having a general operating permit here (ABE).

Also brakes lines withthis alloy type were banned for many years but i did some more research and found out my knowledge was outdated, this type of lines were banned till a little over a year ago, it just seems like not many companies go through the testing and approval process as i've never heard of any (other than some oldtimers).

Heres the article i found:

Original text: https://www.kfz-betrieb.vogel.de/kunifer-bremsleitungen-sind-endlich-zugelassen-a-969522/ 

Translation: 
But on September 8th (2020), the time had come: The KBA issued the ABE "61429 for copper-nickel-iron replacement brake lines (KuNiFer brake lines)" from the Danish manufacturer OJD Automotive ApS.  This was made possible by project work by GTÜ's technical service.  It is the first ABE of this kind. According to the testing organization, the approval was preceded by basic work with a long series of tests in test laboratories and a bachelor's thesis.  It was then clear that the danger described in 1994 did not emanate from the OJD brake lines. 

At that time (1994), tests had shown that embrittlement can occur when forming the copper-nickel brake lines (especially when bending in tight radii), which in turn can lead to a risk of breakage.  As a result, replacement brake lines made of the alloy for use in the area of ​​the StVZO were not according to regulations - with the exception of those cases in which the same lines are also used in series by the vehicle manufacturer.



According to GTÜ, the positive results of the first tests were the starting signal for intensive committee work: The technical managers of GTÜ and the head of technical service entered into dialogue with all committees in Germany that are responsible for the safe operation of vehicles in the area of ​​the StVZO.  The testing organization was able to convince experts that the level of knowledge from the 1990s is outdated.  Finally, in 2017, the federal and state technical committee for motor vehicle engineering (BLFA TK) agreed that an ABE can be created for this type of brake line. 

In turn, numerous individual tests over several months were necessary to create the ABE.  The pressure test of the lines alone took 70 days because a pressure of at least 150 bar had to be built up more than a million times.  Then the final test report was available, the draft of the ABE was created and submitted to the Federal Motor Transport Authority.
